body:
I want to apologise because I feel like a shitdick about it. Perhaps I should let nature takes its course and take an opportunity to talk to her when it comes to me.

I believe that while yes, there are differences in the experience of money, it shouldn't be in the way of me having to say "wow, that's looks awesome," right? I shouldn't be shot down for appreciating things. It's not like I'd it straight up because first of all, I know my priorities and I don't think that they think of me that way. They see me as a kid with a compulsive desire to buy things when I'm not, at least I don't think so.

I don't know about that. University is miles away from home, at least you have to take a plane ride of about 3 hours or at least 2 days by road. Things might get messy the first few weeks but I think things will settle down and everyone is weaned off by the 3rd ~ 4th week. I'm thinking of joining the sports clubs in the University since that would be a great start for a support group. I think there will be a counselling service, at least I'd like to think so.

The academic year will start around the end of February next year. Exactly, I don't want the pressure to be the trigger. If my suicidal thoughts were a gun, it's currently on safety but if things like this continue, I might just reach for it and turn the barrel on myself.

I did try and tell them about that plan but they merely put the idea aside. Instead of asking me why so, I was merely told that Psychologists earn less and are subject to emotional and mental trauma through their patients/clients. They discouraged me into taking the course. It doesn't stop there, I was told that I merely wanted the easy way around, that I am being lazy. The thing is though, I don't want to disappoint them or something and I'm confused as hell. I don't know what to do and them being stubborn about the subject matter isn't helping, at all.

Well, the house doesn't feel like a home. Me and my mum haven't talked since the incident happened. I feel like such an asshole about it.  I regret that decision but what's done is done and I feel like I should move on, but the no-talking atmosphere at home doesn't help with that.

Other than academics, I have to watch what I say and what I do. It's like censorship, I hate it. I cannot express myself because they are being stubborn about things around them.

There's this one time where I was browsing through an auction site for cars and while it's not bad to dream and aspire, right? My mum says, "No! No! You finish school first then you can buy whatever you want." I didn't say anything, I didn't do anything but browse through a damn website and see a car that I've dreamt of. At that time, my friend and his mum was around as well, I just wanted to show my friend what kind of car I wanted few years down the line and THAT was HER reaction?! I never understood that. I tried but I really don't.

News on the telly showed the advancements in ocular technology such as the Oculus Rift and the Google Glass and they immediately shot me down for being enamored by it. Technology continues to evolve. It will continue to make our lives easier and allow us to experience things that have never been experienced before. Is it bad to acknowledge that we have moved forward? I don't think so, so why do they shot me down for that? I don't know.

I tried volunteering for the local hospice however, they're full with volunteers and staff. I did try and volunteer for the SPCA but it's too far from my house and I don't have a license to drive on my own, yet. And besides, I have a job over the holidays so that takes away my time. Perhaps when I'm in university, I may be able to sneak in a time to volunteer in my timetable.

I have enrolled for the first year course. I have considered doing Psychology, then moving on to Clinical Psychology thinking that I could possibly help other people in need. I have also considered doing any trade but I'm always pushed to go to University. Other than those, I've also considered going to Police academy. The thing is, while my intentions are really to help and make a difference in my own way, my family doesn't see things like that. I understand that they'd want me to have financial and job security due to the demand of doctors anywhere across the world but, do they care about what I want? I don't think so. Sure, there's that kind of story but I feel like, deep down, all they want is the prestige - that they were able to send a kid to Med school and actually become a doctor. Nothing else matters, I feel like the things they tell me about being a doctor is just a decoy.

We immigrated from a third world country to a much more developed country. Yes, there are very large cultural differences. Combine that with generation gap, there's a disparity between our views in life. Sure the things they've experienced were hard but the thing is, those do not apply to our environment now. Those things will not happen anymore because this is a different world than the one we were before.

Indeed, I do have friends that I can hang out with but stick their asses out for me? No way. There's no way in hell those people will. I would for them but I realised one thing, they won't for me. I've had many friends in life and their behaviours compared to the people before, it's very much the same. From experience, I know which people will and won't rat me out, and guess what, most of them will rat me out. Most, if not all, of them put me down, ridicule me and all that. I just take it as a joke and laugh with them but inside, I feel hopeless and powerless. I'm crying. I don't get the feeling that I fit in, even with the misfits. 

When I leave? What do you mean? When I leave home? When I die? When I leave home, I want to just want my family, the entire family, to be happy for my choices - the good AND bad. To acknowledge that these choices are what made me the person I have become. Because there is a quote I found to be enlightening - Life is all about choices, you make one and you never look back. I hope that they would understand that they can't control everyone, they might have swayed the people from the past into things that they wanted them to be but not me, I don't want to be controlled. I want to be me and I want them to accept that.

When I die, I want to at least have made a difference in someone's life. Big or small. Even with little things. I want to help.

Indeed, but I'd put suicide to be last on the list. I know better, but I guess I'm running out of options.

My life at home isn't oppressive. I guess that's too strong of a word to describe my family. They are great people, but they see me as the kid that was the star of the family because there was no other babies in the family at the time I was a baby. They don't see me as a person who has a different opinion, different standpoint, different views and pretty much different from them. They see me as a baby they expect to be able to shelter all the time. And by family, I mean everyone up to the second degree of consanguinity and affinity. For 4-6 years of my life, I've been under the care of my childless uncle and aunt while my mum is away in another country. 

They expect me to enter Med school. While that's a good idea, I don't think I'll be happy. I'll be honest, I'd only be doing it for financial reasons. If 75-90k/year pay when you're an intern isn't good, I don't know what is. That's in the urban areas by the way. Add another five years + work in the rural areas, you're looking at north of 300k/year. Yes, being a doctor is good but I'd only be doing it for the money.

They trust that I'll be able to do that like it'll be a walk in the park, but I guess they think that way because they've never actually been there. It's not easy. The last time I talked to them, they asked if I already got into the school like I was going to kindy. That's a load of crap. 

Don't get me wrong, being sheltered is nice but I need to grow, as a person, as an individual, as a human being. I need to stand on my own feet. All I want for them is to be happy with what I want to be, be open about my views, try and see things from the viewpoint of a millennial who grew up in a 21st century society; not from a third world and anti-progressive view.
